newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban leader pays first visit to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban leader pays first visit to Kabul.

text.p: Mullah Mohammad Omar, the reclusive chief of Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia, is visiting Kabul for the first time since his bearded fighters seized it in September, Taleban sources said on Tuesday.

The sources, at Taleban headquarters in the southern city of Kandahar, told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) that Omar had gone to the Afghan capital on Saturday for talks with the ruling interim shura (council) there.
They said Omar would return to his home base in Kandahar after his meetings, but gave no date.

Omar was discussing "recent changes in Afghanistan", the sources said, apparently referring to the Taleban's disastrous defeat last month in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif. On May 19, the Taleban forged a pact with northern General Abdul Malik, who led a mutiny against opposition leader Abdul Rashid Dostum and let Taleban fighters into Mazar-i-Sharif. The pact swiftly fell apart amid fri ction between the Taleban and the northern capital's ethnic Uzbek and Shi'ite Moslem Hazara population. Malik's troops joined the opposition Shi'ite Hezb-i-Wahdat militia to expel the Taleban, who fled the city, leaving at least 300 dead and 700 prisoners.
